questions.q: Describe the Fundamental Rights guaranteed by the Indian Constitution.
answer: The Indian Constitution guarantees six Fundamental Rights in Part III, which are enforceable in the courts.

answer.text: The Right to Equality ensures equality before the law, forbids discrimination, and abolishes untouchability and titles. The Right to Freedom gives citizens freedom of speech, assembly, movement and profession, and protects their life and personal liberty.
The Right against Exploitation bans human trafficking, forced labour and child labour. The Right to Freedom of Religion allows every person to freely profess, practise and propagate any religion.

The Cultural and Educational Rights protect the language, script and institutions of minorities. Finally, the Right to Constitutional Remedies lets a citizen approach the courts to enforce these rights, which Ambedkar called the heart and soul of the Constitution.

answer: Together these rights safeguard the dignity and liberty of citizens.

questions.q: Distinguish between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles of State Policy.
answer: The Constitution contains both Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles, which differ in nature and purpose.

answer.text: Fundamental Rights are contained in Part III and are justiciable, meaning a citizen can go to court if they are violated. They mainly protect the individual against arbitrary state action and are essential for political democracy.

The Directive Principles of State Policy, in Part IV and borrowed from Ireland, are guidelines to the state for creating a just and welfare society. They are non-justiciable, so they cannot be enforced by the courts, but they are held to be fundamental in the governance of the country.
The two are meant to be complementary, together aiming at both political and social and economic democracy.

answer: Thus rights protect the individual, while directives guide the state towards social welfare.
